title: Airlock Digital application control alerts
volume: A few a week once the policies have settled: each blocklisted file, each blocked untrusted file in a user folder and each OTP makes one detection. Expect more during a roll-out, while users still run software the policy hasn't learned.
mdr_note: These detections are yours to work. Sophos MDR doesn't work custom detections, and a case your own case rule opens from them is Managed By Self.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: Three custom detection rules for Airlock Digital Application Control, on the third-party alert records the library's Airlock parsers write. They make a detection when a blocklisted file tries to run, when Airlock blocks an untrusted file in a user or temp folder, and when a one-time password lets an untrusted file run. Each rule matches sensor type Airlock Digital only.
notes:
Setup:
- Add the library's Airlock Digital parsers and an external logging receiver in JSON form in the Airlock console, sending Generic Syslog to the data collector, first, then run the check-your-data search to see execution alerts arrive.

How it works:
- The parser sends Airlock's blocked, blocklisted, audit mode and OTP executions to the third-party alert schema, titled with Airlock's execution type and the file name, such as Airlock Blocklist Execution: psexec.exe.
- The blocklist rule takes Blocklist executions, blocked or in audit mode. A blocklisted file that ran in audit mode wasn't stopped.
- The user folder rule takes blocked executions of files under C:\Users, a Temp folder, /Users or /tmp. A blocked file elsewhere, such as an updater in Program Files, makes none.
- The OTP rule takes executions an OTP allowed. Untrusted files that ran only because a policy is in audit mode make none, since there are many while a policy is built.

Tuning:
- If one file is blocked every day on purpose, leave it out in the query itself, such as and summary !contains 'notes_reader.exe'. A suppression rule would hide Sophos's detections for those computers as well.

Testing:
- In a lab tenant on 2026-11-22, each query returned exactly the sample lines tests.json lists in Data Lake Search, and the rules run offline on the same 9 records agreed. The samples went in with their dates moved to the day before the test, so they fell inside the search's time range.
- As live rules there, each one fired on exactly its sample lines within about two minutes.
- No Sophos detector made a detection on these events.
- Airlock's JSON lines posted to HTTP Ingest on their own were stored as Generic, with only the value of their event key kept, and no parser saw them. With a syslog header in front, as the data collector receives Generic Syslog, every line reached the parsers, so the lab sent them that way.

Known gaps:
- Policy changes and server activity go to ManagementEvent, and executions Airlock allowed go to Process, so they have no rule here.
- An OTP is issued in the Airlock console, which these records don't show: the detection names the file and computer, not who issued the OTP.
